title: Incremental Path-Level Attribution Service for Route/Model/Customer Cost & Latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a scalable service that computes incremental cost and latency attribution at path granularity (route -> model -> customer), capturing shared-cost signals (batching, kernel sharing, KV cache hits/partial hits) and emitting reconciled per-tenant breakdowns for Console dashboards and billing ingestion. The service should support both streaming (near-realtime) and batched rollups with deterministic reconciliation for audits.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Service ingests runtime traces and token-level telemetry and produces per-route/model/customer daily and 5m rollups. 2) Breakdown accounts for shared costs (batch_size attribution, per-GPU occupancy, prefix cache hits) with configurable attribution strategies. 3) Console dashboards display the new breakdown and agree with sample ledger checks within 0.5% for P95 customers. 4) Rollout path and fallback policies exist so we can disable without impacting live billing flows.
tech_notes: - Ingest sources: runtime spans, batching logs, kernel occupancy metrics, prefix cache telemetry, and tenant mapping. - Core compute: streaming engine (Flink/Materialize prototype) for 5m windows + a daily batch reducer. - Attribution model: hybrid weighted split (static weights for kernel/shared items, dynamic weights for batch composition), with ability to plug in ML-based posterior adjustments later. - Storage: columnar time-series for rollups (BigQuery/ClickHouse) + object store for raw window snapshots. - Query patterns: per-tenant historical slicing, anomaly detection, and reconciliation jobs. - Perf targets: compute 5m rollups for 10k routes and 50k tenants within 3 minutes of window close. - Observability: per-job SLOs, data-lag alerts, and sample tracing for reconciliation audits.
data_schema: Flat event-level records with fields: timestamp, request_id, route_id, model_id, tenant_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_id, batch_size, kernel_tag, gpu_ms, kv_cache_hit_count, kv_cache_partial_hit_bytes, raw_cost_nanos, trace_id. Rollup rows: window_start, window_end, route_id, model_id, tenant_id, attributed_cost_nanos, attributed_gpu_ms, attribution_strategy.
migration_plan: 1) Start with read-only rollups for Console: compute and surface in a new dashboard (no billing downstream). 2) Validate against sampled ledger snapshots for 2 weeks. 3) Run side-by-side with existing charge reconciler for another 2 weeks, track divergence alerts. 4) Flip to canonical for analytics queries; only promote to billing path after security/finance signoff.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: backend-only with feature flag (console.usage.attribution.v1) visible to internal users. Phase 2: gated beta for 10 enterprise customers. Phase 3: full rollout and enablement for Reserved/Dedicated customers. Include an emergency kill switch and automatic fallback to coarse attribution algorithm.
test_plan: - Unit tests for attribution math and edge cases (empty batches, partial KV hits). - Integration tests: synthetic runtime event replay and end-to-end rollup validation. - Load test: replay 24h of peak production traffic at 3x speed and measure compute latency and memory. - Acceptance: reconciliation job must pass deterministic checks against golden snapshots.
runbook: - Alert on job lag > 5 minutes or failure rate > 0.5%. - If rollups diverge from ledger > 2% for 12 hours, pause ingestion and run reconciliation. - Steps for emergency disable: flip feature flag, route queries to legacy aggregator, notify finance and on-call infra.
open_questions: How granular should kernel-level cost attribution be for models that share kernels across routes?
Do we prefer deterministic static weights initially or try to infer dynamic weights from observed batch comps?
Where should reconciled rollups be stored for low-latency Console queries vs long-term audits?
